facts.text: The Port of Vancouver handled a record 170.4 million metric tonnes of cargo in 2025, almost 8% more than the previous record set in 2024.
Container volumes through the Port of Vancouver rose 9% in 2025 to 3.78 million TEUs, with laden imports up 5% to 1.91 million TEUs.
British Columbia hosts 40% of all Canadian film and TV production and is the third largest film centre in North America after New York and California.
Family households make up 53% of Vancouver households and one-person households 39%, while the city's after-tax low income rate fell to 13% in 2020 from 19% in 2015.
Vancouver welcomed 11.27 million overnight visitors in 2024, an increase of 3% year over year.

overview: Vancouver had 662,248 residents at the 2021 Census, up 4.9 percent from 631,486 in 2016, packed into just 115.18 square kilometres. That makes it the densest large municipality in Canada, and its 305,336 occupied dwellings are dominated by apartments, so customers live close together and walk, cycle or take transit to nearby businesses.

The port, film and television production, and tourism drive a diverse economy, and many households are single people or couples without children. For a local business, Vancouver offers a huge, affluent and competitive market where standing out in a specific neighbourhood matters more than reaching the entire city.

byService.lead-generation: With 662,248 people in 115.18 square kilometres, Vancouver lead generation should target by neighbourhood and transit corridor, since a customer in Kitsilano rarely travels to Mount Pleasant for the same service.
byService.seo: Vancouver SEO is among the most competitive in Canada, so a business needs neighbourhood landing pages, strong reviews and content aimed at the city's many one-person and newcomer households.
byService.website-development: A Vancouver website must be fast, mobile first and multilingual where it counts, because dense apartment-dwelling customers compare several nearby providers on their phones before choosing.
byService.branding: In a city that grew 4.9 percent between 2016 and 2021 and attracts millions of visitors, Vancouver branding should feel modern and design-conscious while making a clear local, sustainable promise.
